issue: Does the equipoise principle (that a conviction must be reversed when the evidence, viewed in the government's favor, gives equal or nearly equal support to guilt and innocence) remain part of federal sufficiency-of-the-evidence review, and if so, in what form?
provision: Due Process Clause, U.S. Const. amend. V (sufficiency-of-the-evidence review)

sides.position: The equipoise principle remains a helpful tool in sufficiency review and is retained in some form; if the evidence is in equipoise after viewing it in the government's favor, a reasonable jury must entertain a reasonable doubt and the conviction must be reversed.
cases: United States v. Goldesberry, 128 F.4th 1183 (10th Cir. 2025)
United States v. Lovern, 590 F.3d 1095 (10th Cir. 2009)
United States v. Simon, 12 F.4th 1 (1st Cir. 2021)
United States v. Glenn, 312 F.3d 58 (2d Cir. 2002)
United States v. Caseer, 399 F.3d 828 (6th Cir. 2005)
United States v. Johnson, 592 F.3d 749 (7th Cir. 2010)

this_court: Retains the equipoise principle as part of sufficiency review (the court's own position, drawing on Lovern).
quote: We note our sister circuits are divided on how the equipoise principle informs sufficiency review.
cite: United States v. Goldesberry, 128 F.4th 1183 (10th Cir. 2025)
